originalTitle: Behari Lal Engineering raises Rs 90.5 cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
simplifiedContent: Behari Lal Engineering, a company that makes iron and steel, has received Rs 90.48 crore from big investors before its Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO will be open for the public to invest on August 12. The company plans to use the money it raises to upgrade its facilities, expand its operations, install solar panels, and pay off debts. This is important because it shows that big investors are interested in the company, which could make the IPO more attractive to others. The company's IPO will include both new shares being sold and existing shares being offered for sale by current owners.

originalTitle: Sebi proposes to bring all bullion trades under vault management rules
simplifiedContent: India's market regulator, Sebi, is trying to improve how the digital gold market is supervised. They want to make sure all physical gold trades are stored and managed safely, so they're proposing new rules for vault managers. This means that all gold trades will have to follow the same rules as Electronic Gold Receipts, which is a system that already exists. People with an interest in this can give their feedback on the proposal until September 1. This change aims to make the gold market more regulated and secure.

originalTitle: Skytech Infinite to launch Rs 22 crore SME IPO on Aug 14 for fueling bigger automation projects
simplifiedContent: Skytech Infinite Platform, a company that specializes in industrial automation, is planning to sell its shares to the public for the first time through an initial public offering (IPO) on August 14. The company hopes to raise 22.68 crore rupees from this sale. The money will be used to improve its financial situation and expand its business into new areas. This is important because it will help the company take on bigger projects and grow its business. The shares are expected to start trading on the NSE Emerge platform on August 21.

originalTitle: Landmark Cars net profit nearly doubles to  ₹14.5 crore in Q1; revenue rises 22%
simplifiedContent: Landmark Cars, a company that sells cars, made a profit of ₹14.5 crore in the first quarter of the year, which is almost double what they made last year. Their total sales, or revenue, also increased by 22% to ₹1,733 crore. A big part of their sales came from selling Mercedes-Benz cars, which accounted for 38% of their total revenue. The company's stock price went up by 15.4% in June and 10.2% in July, which is a good sign for investors. This increase in profit and revenue is a positive sign for the company and its investors.

originalTitle: Sebi proposes wider FPI access to non-agri commodity derivatives
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is thinking of making a change to help foreign investors participate more in the stock market. Right now, these foreign investors, called FPIs, can only trade certain types of contracts related to non-agricultural commodities like crude oil and natural gas. These contracts are "cash settled", which means they are paid out in money, not actual goods. Sebi's proposal would allow FPIs to trade a wider range of these contracts, giving them more opportunities to invest. This change could make it easier for foreign investors to participate in India's commodity markets.

originalTitle: IFCI Q1 Results: Revenue declines, profit improves sequentially to  ₹60 crore
simplifiedContent: IFCI, a company, recently released its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company made a profit of ₹60.27 crore, which is an improvement from the previous quarter. However, its revenue (the amount of money it made from its activities) decreased by 20% to ₹358 crore compared to the same period last year. This is a concern because the company's financial health, measured by its Capital Risk Adequacy Ratio, is still below what is required by regulations, at -17.58%. Overall, the company's results are mixed, with some improvement in profit but decline in revenue and ongoing financial health concerns.
